plan_a_advantages: Focus on form and cadence development, directly addressing running efficiency.
More frequent, shorter runs allow for better recovery and adaptation.
Reduced risk of overtraining due to the lower overall volume.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates cross-training for overall fitness and injury prevention.
Includes a strength and mobility session, which is beneficial for trail running stability and resilience.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, particularly at this stage. It prioritizes consistent, focused form work with short, easy trail runs, which is crucial for developing efficient running mechanics – a key factor in trail speed. Plan B, while including some cross-training and strength work, relies heavily on very short, almost identical easy runs with extended rest periods, which won't directly translate to improved speed. Plan A’s emphasis on cadence and form will build a stronger foundation for faster running than Plan B’s repetitive, low-intensity volume.
